gloss: to drag in; to pull in (physically)

definitions.gloss: to drag in; to pull in (physically)
definitions.explanation: to forcefully pull or drag something or someone into a place

definitions.gloss: to drag into; to draw into (figuratively)
definitions.explanation: to involve someone in a situation, conflict, or trouble, often against their will

examples.japanese: {重|おも}い{荷物|にもつ}を{部屋|へや}に{引|ひ}きずり{込|こ}んだ。
examples.english: I dragged the heavy luggage into the room.

examples.japanese: {犬|いぬ}が{枝|えだ}を{家|いえ}の{中|なか}に{引|ひ}きずり{込|こ}んできた。
examples.english: The dog dragged a branch into the house.

examples.japanese: {溺|おぼ}れている{人|ひと}を{船|ふね}の{上|うえ}に{引|ひ}きずり{込|こ}んだ。
examples.english: We dragged the drowning person onto the boat.

examples.japanese: {争|あらそ}いに{引|ひ}きずり{込|こ}まれた。
examples.english: I was dragged into a dispute.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{仲間|なかま}を{犯罪|はんざい}に{引|ひ}きずり{込|こ}んだ。
examples.english: He dragged his friends into crime.

examples.japanese: {長期化|ちょうきか}する{裁判|さいばん}に{引|ひ}きずり{込|こ}まれて、{精神的|せいしんてき}に{疲|つか}れてしまった。
examples.english: I was drawn into a prolonged trial and became mentally exhausted.

notes:
A compound verb formed from {引|ひ}きずる (to drag) and {込|こ}む (into). The literal sense describes physical dragging, while the figurative sense describes being pulled into unwanted situations.

TRANSITIVITY:
Transitive. The intransitive equivalent would be a passive construction: {引|ひ}きずり{込|こ}まれる (to be dragged into).

COMMON PATTERNS:
- AをBに{引|ひ}きずり{込|こ}む: to drag A into B
- {引|ひ}きずり{込|こ}まれる: to be dragged in (passive)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {争|あらそ}いに{引|ひ}きずり{込|こ}む: to drag into a dispute
- {泥沼|どろぬま}に{引|ひ}きずり{込|こ}む: to drag into a quagmire
- {犯罪|はんざい}に{引|ひ}きずり{込|こ}む: to drag into crime

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {巻|ま}き{込|こ}む: to involve, to drag in — more general; can be accidental involvement
- {引|ひ}き{込|こ}む: to pull in, to lure in — less forceful than {引|ひ}きずり{込|こ}む
- {引|ひ}きずる: to drag — the base verb, without the "into" direction
